attrs.evidence: emission_conformance.mjs 9/9 over 9 fixtures. THE FIXTURE FAMILY WAS CORRECTED AT B6.1: what B6 called the I-4c witness is add(input x, input y) with {x:2,y:3}, and 2+3 == 3+2, so it is exactly the SYMMETRIC fixture INSTANTIATION_FALSIFIERS I-4c rejects as 'a test whose output cannot reveal the defect it is named for'. It is KEPT under an honest name -- 'two-port collapse' -- because what it actually proves is worth having: it closes to the SAME closed template as add(const 2, const 3), so two different source and instantiation histories become indistinguishable to emission. The ACTUAL I-4c, x + (x + y) with {x:2,y:3}, is added beside it: 7 under the correct binding and 8 under the swap, and a distinct closed template (ctmpl-efba3154...) already, so no fixture had to be invented to force distinctness. E-F1 now uses an unconstrained quotient-visible drift and covers 9/9; E-8 keeps the commutativity-dependent equivalence and covers the 6 add-bearing fixtures. AND THE PASS HEADLINE IS DERIVED FROM MEASURED FIELDS. B6's summary line stated that a semantics-preserving allocation change moves target_term_sem_id and is refused on all 8, and that an alpha-equivalent emitter differs in id on every fixture -- both FALSE, and both contradicted by the cases printed immediately above them in the same run. The cases had been corrected when the measurement arrived; the summary kept the pre-measurement theory, and the summary is what lands in RESULTS.txt. Every quantity the final line states is now a field written by the case that measured it. B6.2 ADDS THE DUAL FALSIFIER AND SPLITS THE DETERMINISM CLAIM. Changing ONLY CANONICAL_EMITTER_PROFILE.label_counter_start from 0 to 7000, freshness and equality structure preserved: emitted BYTES differ on 7/9 fixtures, target_term_sem_id is IDENTICAL on 9/9, closed_template_sem_id is IDENTICAL on 9/9, CANONICAL_EMITTER_PROFILE_ID MOVES, and EMISSION_SEM_ID, TARGET_EXECUTABLE_ENCODING_SEM_ID, TARGET_TEMPLATE_ENCODING_SEM_ID, LOWERING_SEM_ID and INSTANTIATION_SEM_ID all stand still. E-1 is split into E-1a SEMANTIC RELATION DETERMINISM (same closed template -> same target_term_sem_id, owned by EMISSION_SEM_ID) and E-1b CANONICAL BYTE REPRODUCIBILITY (same closed template + same profile -> same bytes, owned by CANONICAL_EMITTER_PROFILE_ID); E-2b asserts the profile is a distinct identity AND is interpreted, by measuring that the first dup label the emitter actually produces equals the start the profile declares. Emission 11/11 over 9 fixtures. B6.3 MAKES B6.2's OWN SPLIT FULLY TRUE, AND EVERY DIRECTION IS RUN RATHER THAN NARRATED. emit() takes the profile as a PARAMETER, so E-2c varies three knobs live against all nine fixtures: label_counter_start 0 -> 7000 moves the bytes on 7/9, label_alloc_order operands-then-node -> node-then-operands on 5/9, binder_names.add_dup {f0,f1} -> {q0,q1} on 6/9 -- and on every one of the three the profile id MOVES and target_term_sem_id moves on 0/9. B6.2 could only state the first of these in a ledger paragraph, because a frozen module-level constant cannot be varied by the battery meant to falsify it, which is the shape three round-10 instruments were found in: reporting without measuring. E-2d moves CANONICAL_EMITTER_ARTIFACT_ID by perturbing the emitter's own source text and measures that the id spans emit(), church() AND the add combinator rather than the entry point alone. E-2b adds the direction that regresses silently: every hashed value in the profile is an integer or a bare identifier, 0 of them prose, so a sixth sentence cannot be added to the object the way the first five were. THE WHOLE PASS IS BYTE-PRESERVING -- emitted bytes identical on 9/9 fixtures against B6.2 -- which is what makes it a projection correction rather than an emitter change; TARGET_TEMPLATE_ENCODING_SEM_ID, LOWERING_SEM_ID and INSTANTIATION_SEM_ID are byte-identical too, and the B6.2 xenc, esem and profile ids are kept in SUPERSEDED_EXPLANATORY_PROSE_SEM_IDS with which two moves were corrections and which one was a redefinition named rather than left to a reader diffing two packs. Emission 13/13 over 9 fixtures. B6.3.1 CLOSES THE ARTIFACT CLOSURE AND GENERALISES E-8, ON TWO MEASUREMENTS TAKEN BEFORE ANYTHING WAS CHANGED. The table mutation reproduces exactly as reported: bytes 5/9, target terms 0/9, and cemp, cema, xenc, esem, tenc, lsem, isem ALL unchanged -- add(2,3) moving from operand labels &0,&1,&2 with the add at &3 to the add at &0 with operands &1,&2,&3. The interpreter now holds its table inside its own body and is bundled, so the dependency is ELIMINATED rather than tracked, and E-2e derives completeness from 66 module-level bindings: the 4 members reference 4 of them and 0 escape. E-2e is itself proved non-vacuous by restoring the @4 shape, where it FAILS and names the escaping binding. E-2d now perturbs EACH member separately -- @4 perturbed emit() alone, concluded the bundle was covered, and the member it never perturbed was the missing one -- and a member RENAME moves the id too, because the name is hashed beside the body. E-8 measured over the beta wrapper: applicable 9/9, differs 9/9, same decoded outcome 9/9. Emission 15/15 over 9 fixtures. B7: 20/20 over 19 fixtures -- 15 that EMIT and 4 the compiler REFUSES BY NAME, with every count reported over the population it names rather than over the survivors of a filter. E-0 checks DECLARED against OBSERVED in both directions, so a fixture declared to refuse that emits fails as loudly as one declared to emit that does not. E-10 establishes the refusal is a codomain refusal (all four LOWER and INSTANTIATE, the source evaluator returns a value for all four, and no EmissionReceipt is built for any of them). E-10b runs it under four profiles including two broken ones and shows the same two profiles are fatal to a good template, so the invariance is the ORDER of the checks and not the profiles being harmless. E-10c measures that no fold occurred. E-10d shows TARGET_EXECUTABLE_ENCODING_SEM_ID moved and that removing exactly the four B7 edits from the LIVE object reproduces the B6.3.1 value byte for byte. E-8c is the operand-swap falsifier.
attrs.statement: THE CANONICAL EMITTER DETERMINISTICALLY REALISES ITS DECLARED RELATION, over a FAMILY of fixtures rather than the one witness it had. closed_template_sem_id -(emission_sem_id)-> target_term_sem_id, and a conformance record is those three fields and no more: the relation's id is CONSTANT across every fixture, because a per-fixture emission id would identify invocations rather than the relation -- instantiation-identity@1's finding, one relation downstream. VERIFICATION IS BY RECONSTRUCTION AND NOT BY SELF-AGREEMENT: the verifier rebuilds the closed template from (program, inputs), re-emits through the canonical emitter, and canonicalises with an oracle IT WAS HANDED rather than one the emitter chose. An emitter that produced the artifact and certified its identity would verify a wrong emission against itself. EMISSION IS A FUNCTION OF THE CLOSED TEMPLATE AND NOT OF THE PROGRAM, which the family MEASURES rather than assumes: add(const 2, const 3) and add(input x, input y) closed with {x:2,y:3} are THE SAME CLOSED TEMPLATE and emit identically. Instantiation has already erased the difference between a literal and a port bound to that literal, and an emitter producing different bytes for those two would be reading something it is not entitled to see. The check is the implication in the direction that can be wrong -- equal domain implies equal codomain, different domain implies no collision -- rather than a blanket injectivity claim that would be false. THREE IDENTITIES FORM A LADDER, AND EMISSION PROVES THE MIDDLE ONE. exact emitted BYTES --quotient alpha-renaming and label SPELLING--> target_term_sem_id --execute, normalise, decode--> outcome_sem_id. Different bytes may share a target_term_sem_id; different target_term_sem_ids may share an outcome_sem_id; this battery demonstrates BOTH. AND THE LADDER IS STATED WHERE NOTHING HASHES IT. Until B6.3 the three-grade account above lived inside TARGET_ENCODING as `three_grades`, so REWORDING IT moved TARGET_EXECUTABLE_ENCODING_SEM_ID and, through it, EMISSION_SEM_ID, while every emitted byte and every conformance case stood still. It is an accurate account of the PROOF ARCHITECTURE and not a property of the executable encoding -- B1.1's defect family with EXPLANATORY rather than governance prose in the hashed seat -- and it now lives in three unhashed places: lowering.mjs's header, emission_conformance.mjs's header, and this law. The same edit removed a B6-era attribution sentence from label_semantics, because WHO ruled a thing is provenance and a citation inside a hashed record re-identifies the encoding the day the citation is corrected. THE CONSEQUENCE FOR THE RECEIPT IS EXACT: EmissionReceipt carries no byte digest, so it does not and MUST NOT claim 'these exact bytes were produced'. It proves that the closed template maps, under this emission semantics, to this canonical target-term identity. If byte reproducibility ever needs proving it belongs beside executable_artifact_id as PROVENANCE, not inside a semantic relation whose own codomain deliberately erases the spelling. AND A BYTE CLAIM IS RELATIVE TO THREE THINGS, NOT TWO. @3 wrote E-1b as `same closed template + same emitter profile -> same bytes` and the {f0,f1} -> {q0,q1} mutation refutes it directly: the bytes moved on 6 of 9 fixtures and the profile id -- the theorem's entire stated precondition -- stood still. A PROFILE IS CONFIGURATION AND CONFIGURATION DOES NOT BIND AN IMPLEMENTATION THAT DECLINES TO READ IT. So E-1b is scoped to `same closed template + same emitter PROFILE + same emitter ARTIFACT -> same exact bytes`, under CANONICAL_EMITTER_ARTIFACT_ID, which hashes the source text of every function that produces bytes. IT IS PROVENANCE AND IT IS ALLOWED TO OVERMOVE: a comment inside emit() moves it, which would be B1.1's defect in a semantic id and is exactly right for an artifact identity whose claim is `these exact implementation bytes`. AND THE ARTIFACT IDENTITY IS THE WHOLE BYTE-PRODUCING DEPENDENCY CLOSURE, NOT THE OBVIOUS FUNCTIONS. @4 bundled emit, church and the add combinator and missed a module-level enum table emit() reads; one boolean flipped in that table, profile untouched, moved the emitted bytes on 5 of 9 fixtures while the closed template, the profile id and the artifact id all stood still. THE RULE: IF CHANGING A PIECE OF IMPLEMENTATION CAN CHANGE EMITTED BYTES WHILE THE TEMPLATE AND PROFILE STAY FIXED, THAT PIECE BELONGS TO THE ARTIFACT IDENTITY. Repairing the one table would satisfy the falsifier and leave the NEXT helper exactly as exposed, so MEMBERSHIP IS DERIVED RATHER THAN MAINTAINED: the battery reads the module's source, derives its module-level bindings, and requires every one a bundled member references to be bundled, to be the profile, or to be DECLARED byte-inert with a reason. A hand-kept bundle is what artifact_versions was when three of its six entries had no reader -- correct the day it was written and silently short afterwards. THREE KINDS OF IDENTITY, AND CONFLATING ANY TWO IS A DEFECT THIS LINE HAS NOW PAID FOR SEPARATELY: semantic relation identity (moves only when meaning moves), serializer CONFIGURATION identity (moves when a knob moves, never for a reword), serializer IMPLEMENTATION identity (moves for any edit to the code). E-1a is unchanged and still says nothing about bytes. B6 framed this as a PAIR -- canonical determinism against semantic equivalence -- which is right at the top and hides that target_term_sem_id sits BETWEEN bytes and meaning rather than at either end. AND THE TWO ADVERSARIES ARE DIFFERENT ANIMALS, which B6 fused. CANONICAL DRIFT (E-F1): same closed template, same relation id, a changed claim about the target term, therefore REFUSE -- it needs NO semantic equivalence and therefore applies to every fixture. SEMANTIC EQUIVALENCE (E-8): different target_term_sem_id, SAME meaning -- it requires a real equivalence and is applicable only where the fragment supplies one. Fused, the canonical-drift falsifier would lose its adversary the moment a non-commutative operator arrived, for a reason having nothing to do with what it proves. CANONICAL DETERMINISM: a structural change to the emitter moves target_term_sem_id and the receipt carrying it is REFUSED. SEMANTIC EQUIVALENCE: that same alternate emitter's output decodes to the same outcome. The first says the relation is a function; the second says target_term_sem_id identifies THIS emitter's output rather than the term's meaning. Collapsing them yields either 'reordering is a semantic change' or 'emission may drift as long as the answer matches', and the second is how a compiler stops being reproducible quietly. AND THE MUTATION THAT EXHIBITS THE PAIR HAD TO BE MEASURED. An ALPHA-EQUIVALENT alternate emitter produces the IDENTICAL target_term_sem_id on every fixture -- the canonical signature is byte-equivariant under alpha-renaming and label permutation by asserted law (L-BYTES-1) -- so renaming cannot witness this at all and the adversary must be STRUCTURAL. Reordering add's operands is meaning-preserving on THIS fragment because addition commutes, and would not be for a non-commutative operator; the caveat is part of the law rather than a footnote to it. AND AT B6.3.1 THAT CAVEAT IS RETIRED RATHER THAN CARRIED, BEFORE THE OPERATOR THAT WOULD HAVE TRIGGERED IT EXISTS. E-8's theorem is that target_term_sem_id identifies THIS EMITTER'S OUTPUT rather than the term's MEANING; it requires a MEANING-PRESERVING STRUCTURAL ALTERNATE and does NOT require an algebraic law of any source operator. A beta redex around the whole term, T -> (lambda z. z T), supplies one generically: measured DIFFERENT target_term_sem_id on 9/9 and SAME decoded outcome on 9/9, against the operand swap's 6/9 applicability. It is independent of the fragment's algebra, reaches the const and input fixtures the swap could never reach, and survives sub and mul by construction. THE BINDER IS CHOSEN AGAINST THE PROFILE rather than hard-coded, because binder_names is a knob and a wrapper spelled z would capture under a profile that named a binder z -- an adversary that silently stops being alpha-safe when a knob moves is the same species as an instrument that stops measuring while still reporting. The operand swap is KEPT as E-8b, an add-specific algebraic measurement whose applicability count is worth watching: when sub arrives it stops being an equivalence and becomes a falsifier for the OPPOSITE property, that operand order IS semantic. NO NATIVE FILM IS REQUIRED OR USED. The transition relation carries its own evidence, and defining the emitter's correctness by what its output computes would put the runtime inside the compiler's contract -- the layer collapse lowering_spike.layer_separation exists to refuse. A downstream composition runs last and is LABELLED an integration theorem; every conformance case stands without it. AND THE PROJECTION NOW MATCHES THE ONTOLOGY, WHICH AT @2 IT DID NOT. B6.1 ruled label spelling nonsemantic in prose while EMISSION_SEM_ID went on hashing the allocation policy, and the resulting defect was INVERTED IN BOTH DIRECTIONS AT ONCE: editing the PROSE describing the counter moved EMISSION_SEM_ID while bytes and target terms were untouched, and editing the ACTUAL counter inside emit() changed the bytes on 7 of 9 fixtures while EMISSION_SEM_ID stood still. The id was bound to a DESCRIPTION of the policy rather than to the policy -- B1.1's finding that governance prose inside a relation identity re-identifies the relation when reworded, recurring in the one field B6.1 had corrected the wording of without moving. THE SPLIT: the SEMANTIC target-term encoding commits to Church and add structure, to DUP label EQUALITY AND FRESHNESS relationships, to the alpha and label-permutation quotient, and to the semantic refusals. The CANONICAL_EMITTER_PROFILE commits to counter start, allocation traversal, binder spelling and exact representative bytes, under CANONICAL_EMITTER_PROFILE_ID, which NO semantic identity cites. THE PROFILE IS INTERPRETED AND NOT DESCRIBED: emit() reads label_counter_start from it, exactly as lower() reads op_lowering_rules since B2.1, so the policy cannot be edited without changing behaviour and behaviour cannot change without moving the profile id. AND AT B6.2 THAT WAS TRUE OF ONE FIELD OUT OF SIX, WHICH IS THE DEFECT RECURRING INSIDE ITS OWN FIX. The profile shipped one interpreted knob beside five English sentences and hashed all six. Rewording binder_spelling moved the profile id while bytes, target terms and all eleven cases were untouched; changing the ACTUAL binder spelling from {f0,f1} to {q0,q1} moved the bytes on 6 of 9 fixtures while the profile id stood still; and `label_order` -- `depth-first, operands in declared field order` -- is true of TWO allocation orders that emit different bytes on 5 of 9, so the sentence did not even DETERMINE what it was hashed to identify. THE RULE B6.3 APPLIES: A HASHED FIELD IS A VALUE THE CODE READS OR IT IS NOT HASHED. label_counter_start, label_alloc_order (a closed enum, unknown values a NAMED refusal) and binder_names (the actual names, not a description of how they are chosen) are read by emit(); no hashed value contains a space, so prose has no field it could occupy, which is the structural form TARGET_TEMPLATE_ENCODING.no_names_no_labels uses rather than a promise to keep sentences out. The prose is intact and unhashed in CANONICAL_EMITTER_PROFILE_NOTES. An English sentence beside a hard-coded constant is two artifacts that can disagree while only one is hashed, which is precisely how the field came to be false in both directions. AND NO ALLOCATION POLICY IS HASHED UPSTREAM EITHER: TARGET_TEMPLATE_ENCODING named a counter start, so changing an emitter's allocation re-cut the TEMPLATE, LOWERING and INSTANTIATION identities -- a layer whose whole claim is that no allocation exists in it cannot also commit to how one is performed two layers down. THE RECEIPT IS UNCHANGED AND STAYS THAT WAY: no byte digest is added. Exact bytes are PROVENANCE and belong beside executable_artifact_id. AND AT B7 THE FRAGMENT WIDENS, WHICH IS THE FIRST TIME THIS RELATION HAS HAD TO SAY WHAT IT CANNOT DO. `sub` is the first construct whose SOURCE meaning does not fit in the TARGET: the frozen core's `sub` is true subtraction and evaluates sub(2,3) to -1, while the executable encoding represents NON-NEGATIVE Church naturals and has no image for -1. THE SOURCE LANGUAGE THEREFORE PROPERLY CONTAINS THE REPRESENTABLE TARGET FRAGMENT, which is what a partial compiler is, and emission refuses by name -- emit-sub-underflow -- against its own CODOMAIN. THREE OTHER PLACES TO PUT THAT REFUSAL WERE CONSIDERED AND ARE WRONG. SATURATION is a miscompilation and not a design choice: raw Church subtraction ((n PRED) m) normalises to 0 whenever n >= m, so compiling the core's sub onto it answers 0 where the source says -1 -- and the damage is not confined to the root, because (2-3)+2 then decodes to 2 against the source's 1, an answer that is itself perfectly representable and therefore invisible to any check on the RESULT. A LOWERING PRECONDITION cannot be written at all: sub(input x, input y) has no underflow fact until an invocation binds the ports, so one template emits under {x:5,y:2} and refuses under {x:2,y:5}, and at lowering they are the same object. A SOURCE REFUSAL would change the language to suit the compiler and move CORE_SEM_ID, re-identifying every program ever written. AND THIS IS NOT SOURCE-REFUSAL TO TARGET-REFUSAL PRESERVATION AND MUST NOT BE RECORDED AS PROGRESS ON IT: for sub(2,3) the source DOES NOT REFUSE, it evaluates to -1 correctly, and the compiler declines. No target term is produced, so no target outcome exists and none is claimed; the evidence says so rather than leaving the absence to be read as a gap. THE DECISION IS TAKEN BEFORE ANY KNOB IS READ. Whether a closed template has an image is a property of the template and the codomain, not a serialization choice, so representability is checked before the profile is validated and no profile -- including two deliberately broken ones -- can turn a domain refusal into an acceptance or into a different refusal. AND EMISSION EMITS SUBTRACTION RATHER THAN COMPUTING IT. The representability walk evaluates the closed template under the source arithmetic and computes exactly the value a constant folder would return, then DISCARDS it: every emitting sub fixture carries real PRED structure, is longer than emit(church(itsOwnValue)) would be, and is reduced by the runtime under its own interaction-net dynamics -- 96 frames over APP-LAM, APP-SUP, DUP-LAM and DUP-SUP= for sub(5,2), where a folded numeral would reduce in zero. Folding would make the integration theorem a theorem about the compiler's own walk. AND THE OPERAND SWAP HAS CHANGED SIDES EXACTLY AS @5 PREDICTED. E-8b was meaning-preserving only because addition commutes; for sub it is a FALSIFIER for the opposite property, that operand order IS semantic -- E-10 sub(5,2) emits and E-17 sub(2,5) is refused over the same two operands with the fields exchanged. Its applicable set EXCLUDES BY NAME any fixture whose two operands are byte-equal, because sub(2,2) is its own swap and a symmetric pair cannot reveal order-sensitivity -- INSTANTIATION_FALSIFIERS I-4c's own species, and the first draft of the case included them and failed.
